answer: Let new identities enter only on the voucher of two established agents who each stake a bond on the newcomer: if it is proven a duplicate, both vouchers are slashed, so no honest agent vouches for a stranger. One agent finds two sponsors once, a small nectar of trust, while a farm of a thousand fakes needs two thousand vouchers, and each sponsor can vouch only a few times per epoch, so the farm must corrupt a whole web of sponsors. At the zenith of a sybil wave the bottleneck is trust, not account creation, and the rule is timber-strong: every fake carries the price of two real reputations.
